newsitem.title: BELGIUM: OLOs to trend lower on economy, Emu worries.
newsitem.headline: OLOs to trend lower on economy, Emu worries.

text.p: Belgian linear bonds are seen trending gently lower for the rest of the week as uncertainties about the French parliament vote, Bundesbank gold and the health of the U.S. and European economies keep buyers sidelined.
The bond market continued Wednesday's selloff on Thursday, but the OLO/Bund spread remained stable around eight bp.
"There are just too many uncertainties around. People don't know what to do and therefore prefer not to take long positions," one dealer said.
Potential for spread-tightening was seen limited by potential short-selling from foreign players.
Dealers said that London players sold OLOs against Bunds as soon as the spread moved towards five bp.
One dealer said the long end of the curve remained well bid, preventing the OLO market from following the 5-10 year steepening trend seen in Germany.
The 5-10 year OLO yield differential was 107 bp in early trade, compared to 120 in Germany.
The franc remained relatively weak at 20.6430/40 to the mark, keeping one-week repos, at 3.31/34 percent, well above the 3.00 percent official central rate.
-- Geert De Clercq, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6813, Fax +32 2 230 7710
